issues.title: Dimension factor in the Fourier-CUR error bound
issues.failure_explanation: Let B=A-EF* have dimensions m=2I_1+1 and n=2I_2+1. Orthonormality of the Fourier basis gives the exact identity between the Fourier-polynomial L2 error and ||B||_F, not an upper bound by ||B||_max. No active hypothesis restricts B to one nonzero entry. The available matrix theorem controls only ||B||_max, so the valid universal conversion is ||B||_F <= sqrt(mn)||B||_max. Consequently, the old proof cannot derive the dimension-free term epsilon||A||_2.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's dimension-free low-rank approximation term is not established and may understate the Fourier L2 error by a factor up to sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)). The later maximal-volume CUR corollary inherits the same omitted factor; the underlying matrix maximum-norm bounds are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use Parseval to state the exact identity ||tilde F f-Ff||_{L2}=||A-EF*||_F, followed by ||A-EF*||_F <= sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1))||A-EF*||_max. Accordingly, multiply the epsilon||A||_2 term in the main approximation theorem and the matrix-residual term in the dependent maximal-volume CUR corollary by sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)), and update their proofs. The underlying maximum-norm matrix bounds need no change.
issues.why_classification: The proof makes an invalid norm inference, and the correction removes a coherent dimension-free error guarantee by introducing an unbounded dimension factor, so this is neither a typo nor a no-loss minor repair. Nevertheless, Parseval and the standard Frobenius-to-maximum-norm conversion provide a contained complete repair: the hypotheses, approximation constructions, rank bound, and form of both affected results remain recognizably comparable, with no global proof reconstruction.
